title: Intentra
tagline: Intentra finds the right human. USDC escrow makes sure they get paid.
description:
Intentra is a decentralized service marketplace , framed as an "AI Commerce Protocol." Here's how it works:

AI-driven matching – you describe what you need and your budget, and an AI parses your intent to find a matching service provider, with the arrangement secured by EIP-712 cryptographic mandates (structured, signed data commitments).
Human verification – providers must prove they're real humans (not bots) using World ID's "World Selfie Check," aiming to eliminate scams and fake accounts.
Escrowed payments
 funds are held in USDC via a smart contract escrow on the Arc testnet, only releasing to the provider once the job is completed and approved by the client.

In short, it's a trust layer for hiring freelancers/service providers where an AI agent handles the negotiation/matching, identity is verified cryptographically, and payment is escrowed on-chain until work is confirmed done.
how_its_made:
The backend is a FastAPI modular monolith, organised domain-per-package rather than
by layer: intents, providers, transactions, authorization, payments, fulfillment,
evidence, disputes, identity and audit each own their router, models, schemas and
service. Boundaries are not a convention here, they are CI — 14 import-linter
contracts fail the build if a domain touches another domain's tables, if the shared
kernel imports a domain, if an adapter reaches back inward, or if pure rule code
(money, hashing, state machine, policy) imports FastAPI, SQLAlchemy or web3. The one
deliberate exception is the Transaction aggregate root, and a test walks the source
tree to prove the state machine is its only writer.

SQLModel/SQLAlchemy async over asyncpg, Alembic migrations, 20 tables. Three worker
loops (chain watcher, transaction outbox, reconciliation) run in-process, guarded by
a Postgres advisory lock so only one instance is leader and the same code scales to
several replicas untouched. 572 tests.

ON-CHAIN

IntentraEscrow is Solidity on Arc testnet (chain 5042002), built with Foundry. Two
rules drive the whole design: money states commit only on confirmed chain events,
never on an optimistic write, and settlement needs two distinct signatures from
{customer, provider, AI arbitrator}. The watcher reads eth_getLogs from the escrow's
deploy block, advances a cursor only after every log in a range is handled, and keys
events on (tx_hash, log_index) so a replay after a crash is a no-op. Outbound calls
go through an outbox: rows are claimed with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, the
transaction hash is committed to the database before we wait for a receipt, and one
lock serialises the resolver's nonce.

PARTNER TECHNOLOGIES

Arc — escrow and settlement in USDC, with gas paid in USDC too, which removes the
"buy the native token first" step that kills onboarding for the Nigerian users this
targets. Deterministic finality let us run the watcher at 1 confirmation.

Privy — email login to an embedded wallet, so a customer signs an EIP-712 mandate
without ever seeing a seed phrase; also signTypedData and sendTransaction for the
escrow calls. Access tokens are ES256-verified server-side against the app's
verification key.

World — Selfie Check proof-of-human gates authorisation and complaint, the two
places fraud pays. One nullifier per action per transaction, so a proof cannot be
replayed onto another job.

The Graph — a subgraph over the escrow's own events turns completed, disputed and
refunded jobs into provider trust scores, so reputation comes from chain history
rather than rows we could edit.
auto_summary: A decentralized service marketplace matches clients with providers, verifies human identity, and settles escrowed USDC payments through an onchain contract.
